entities.name: Scrub Typhus
entities.description: Acute life-threatening zoonotic febrile illness caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi and transmitted by larval trombiculid mites (chiggers), characterized by disseminated endothelial microvascular infection, perivascular cuffing vasculitis, and potential multiorgan failure.

entities.name: Acute Febrile Illness
entities.description: Abrupt onset of high spiking remittent or continuous fever (39-40.5 C) accompanied by violent chills and prostration.

entities.name: Noncardiogenic Pulmonary Edema
entities.description: Extravasation of fluid into alveolar spaces secondary to systemic endothelial permeability breakdown without elevated capillary wedge pressure.

entities.name: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
entities.description: Severe life-threatening hypoxemic respiratory failure characterized by bilateral diffuse alveolar infiltrates and refractory hypoxia.

entities.name: Interstitial Pneumonitis
entities.description: Mononuclear inflammatory cell infiltration and perivascular cuffing within pulmonary interalveolar septa.

entities.name: Acute Kidney Injury
entities.description: Rapid decline in glomerular filtration rate with rising serum creatinine and oliguria secondary to septic vasculitis.

entities.name: Acute Tubular Necrosis
entities.description: Destruction of renal tubular epithelial cells induced by severe ischemic hypoperfusion and systemic microcirculatory collapse.

entities.name: Acute Interstitial Nephritis
entities.description: Direct peritubular capillary vasculitis and lymphocytic infiltration within the renal parenchymal interstitium.

entities.name: Aseptic Meningoencephalitis
entities.description: Central nervous system infection causing encephalic dysfunction, altered consciousness, delirium, and meningismus.

entities.name: Aseptic Meningitis
entities.description: Inflammatory irritation of the leptomeninges without pyogenic bacteria, causing headache, photophobia, and positive meningeal signs.

entities.name: Encephalopathy
entities.description: Global brain dysfunction presenting with drowsiness, psychomotor agitation, confusion, or coma.

entities.name: Infectious Myocarditis
entities.description: Inflammation of cardiac myocytes and myocardial interstitial microvasculature leading to arrhythmias and systolic impairment.

entities.name: Cardiogenic Shock
entities.description: Severe circulatory failure caused by depressed intrinsic myocardial contractility and left ventricular pump failure.

entities.name: Septic Shock
entities.description: Persistent arterial hypotension requiring vasopressors to maintain MAP >= 65 mmHg despite adequate fluid resuscitation.

entities.name: Multiorgan Dysfunction Syndrome
entities.description: Simultaneous progressive physiological failure of multiple vital organ systems resulting from systemic microvascular angiitis.

entities.name: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation
entities.description: Systemic consumptive coagulopathy characterized by microvascular thrombosis, thrombocytopenia, and bleeding diathesis.

entities.name: Acute Pericarditis
entities.description: Inflammation of the pericardial sac layers producing positional retrosternal chest pain and pericardial friction rubs.

entities.name: Pericardial Effusion
entities.description: Accumulation of exudative fluid within the pericardial cavity secondary to serosal endothelial permeability leak.

entities.name: Generalized Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Enlargement of multiple non-contiguous peripheral lymph node basins across cervical, axillary, and inguinal regions.

entities.name: Splenomegaly
entities.description: Pathological enlargement of the spleen resulting from lymphoid hyperplasia and reticuloendothelial clearance of infected cells.

entities.name: Hepatomegaly
entities.description: Enlargement of the liver caused by sinusoidal endothelial swelling, Kupffer cell activation, and perivascular inflammation.

entities.name: Acute Hepatitis
entities.description: Hepatic inflammation characterized by sinusoidal endothelial infection, focal hepatocyte necrosis, and elevated transaminases.

entities.name: Canalicular Cholestasis
entities.description: Impairment of bile excretion secondary to periportal inflammation and sinusoidal endothelial swelling.

entities.name: Gastrointestinal Mucosal Hemorrhage
entities.description: Extensive bleeding from the stomach or intestine caused by submucosal vasculitis, petechiae, and mucosal ulcerations.

entities.name: Multiple Gastric Ulcers
entities.description: Diffuse shallow mucosal erosions and ulcerations throughout the gastric mucosa identified on endoscopy.

entities.name: Acute Pancreatitis
entities.description: Acute inflammation of the pancreas marked by elevated serum amylase/lipase and severe epigastric pain.

entities.name: Severe Frontal Cephalalgia
entities.description: Excruciating, incapacitating frontal or retro-orbital headache caused by cerebral endothelial activation and intracranial vasculitis.

entities.name: Retro-Orbital Pain
entities.description: Deep aching orbital discomfort aggravated by eye movement secondary to local ocular microvascular inflammation.

entities.name: Generalized Myalgia
entities.description: Widespread muscle aches, tenderness, and stiffness involving the back, neck, thighs, and calves.

entities.name: Peripheral Polyneuropathy
entities.description: Peripheral nerve trunk dysfunction caused by ischemia of the vasa nervorum secondary to systemic vasculitis.

entities.name: Acute Transient Deafness
entities.description: Sudden onset of reversible bilateral or unilateral sensorineural hearing impairment.

entities.name: Tinnitus
entities.description: Subjective sensation of ringing, buzzing, or hissing sound in the ears accompanying cochlear microvasculitis.

entities.name: Cranial Nerve Palsy
entities.description: Peripheral cranial nerve dysfunction, most frequently involving cranial nerves VII, VI, or VIII.

entities.name: Cerebral Angiitis
entities.description: Inflammation and mononuclear cuffing of cerebral microvessels and arterioles.

entities.name: Generalized Seizures
entities.description: Paroxysmal motor convulsive activity provoked by severe cortical inflammation, cerebral edema, or high fever.

entities.name: Oliguria
entities.description: Marked reduction in daily urinary output (<400 mL/day or <0.5 mL/kg/h) signaling severe renal impairment.

entities.name: Pleuritic Chest Pain
entities.description: Sharp thoracic pain intensified by inspiration, coughing, or deep breathing secondary to pleural inflammation.

entities.name: Exudative Pleural Effusion
entities.description: Protein-rich fluid accumulation in the pleural space caused by increased pulmonary microvascular permeability.

entities.name: Hypovolemic Hypotension
entities.description: Depressed blood pressure resulting from extensive plasma extravasation into extravascular compartments.

entities.name: Metabolic Lactic Acidosis
entities.description: Elevated blood lactate (>2.0-4.0 mmol/L) with acidemia resulting from inadequate tissue microcirculatory oxygen delivery.

entities.name: Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis
entities.description: Life-threatening hyperinflammatory cytokine storm syndrome characterized by uncontrolled macrophage activation and hemophagocytosis.

entities.name: Necrotic Black Eschar
entities.description: Pathognomonic skin crust resembling a cigarette burn with a black necrotic center surrounded by an erythematous halo.

entities.name: Groin Cutaneous Eschar
entities.description: Necrotic black cigarette-burn crust located in the inguinal crease, scrotum, or perineum.

entities.name: Axillary Inoculation Eschar
entities.description: Necrotic feeding lesion located deep within the moist axillary skin folds.

entities.name: Inframammary Fold Eschar
entities.description: Necrotic black chigger feeding crust concealed under the breast tissue along brassiere compression lines.

entities.name: Waistband Inoculation Eschar
entities.description: Necrotic cutaneous crust located around the beltline, umbilical fold, or lower abdomen.

entities.name: Perineal Inoculation Eschar
entities.description: Painless necrotic black crust situated on the perineal or perianal skin folds.

entities.name: Regional Tender Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Painful, tender enlargement of the sentinel lymph node chain anatomically draining the cutaneous eschar.

entities.name: Sensorineural Hearing Loss
entities.description: Acute reversible cochlear or acoustic nerve sensory hearing deficit appearing during acute infection.

entities.name: Centrifugal Maculopapular Exanthem
entities.description: Transient erythematous maculopapular rash developing on the trunk and spreading centrifugally to limbs.

entities.name: Bulbar Conjunctival Suffusion
entities.description: Prominent bilateral bulbar conjunctival erythema and vascular engorgement without purulent discharge.

entities.name: Subconjunctival Hemorrhage
entities.description: Focal scleral extravasation of blood resulting from severe microvascular capillary disruption.

entities.name: Relative Bradycardia
entities.description: Pulse-temperature dissociation (Faget sign) where pulse rate is inappropriately low for the degree of fever.

entities.name: Meningismus
entities.description: Clinical signs of meningeal irritation including nuchal rigidity, Kernig sign, and Brudzinski sign.

entities.name: Palpable Splenic Tip
entities.description: Soft, slightly tender splenic margin palpated beneath the left costal margin on deep inspiration.

entities.name: Tender Hepatomegaly
entities.description: Enlarged liver with smooth edge exhibiting tenderness on manual palpation.

entities.name: Facial Flushing
entities.description: Prominent plethoric erythema over the cheeks, forehead, and periorbital tissues during early high fever.

entities.name: Cutaneous Petechiae
entities.description: Non-blanching pinpoint intradermal hemorrhages on the trunk and extremities reflecting microvascular fragility.

entities.name: Fine Basilar Crackles
entities.description: High-pitched end-inspiratory crackles auscultated over the lower posterior lung fields.

entities.name: Postauricular Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Enlarged, tender lymph nodes located behind the mastoid process.

entities.name: Inguinal Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Painful, tender enlargement of superficial inguinal lymph nodes in the groin basin.

entities.name: Erythematous Maculopapular Papule
entities.description: Initial painless, non-pruritic erythematous papule or vesicle marking the early chigger feeding site.

entities.name: Altered Mental Status
entities.description: Acute delirium, confusion, psychomotor slowing, or obtundation during high-grade fever.

entities.name: Peripheral Edema
entities.description: Pitting edema involving the pretibial regions and ankles resulting from hypoalbuminemia and capillary leak.

entities.name: Scleral Icterus
entities.description: Yellow discoloration of the sclera indicating elevated conjugated and total bilirubin.

entities.name: Tachypnea
entities.description: Elevated respiratory rate (>20-24 breaths/minute) signaling respiratory distress or metabolic compensation.

entities.name: Dry Cough
entities.description: Persistent non-productive cough reflecting bronchial perivascular inflammation.

entities.name: Resting Tachycardia
entities.description: Inappropriate heart rate elevation (>100 bpm) at rest signaling sepsis compensation or myocarditis.

entities.name: Hypotensive Shock
entities.description: Severe drop in systolic blood pressure (<90 mmHg) accompanied by cold clammy extremities.

entities.name: Mild Neutrophilic Leukocytosis
entities.description: White blood cell count mildly elevated between 10,000 and 14,000/uL with neutrophilic predominance.

entities.name: Normal Leukocyte Count
entities.description: Total white blood cell count within normal reference range (4,000-10,000/uL) despite high fever.

entities.name: Prominent Bandemia
entities.description: Presence of immature non-segmented neutrophils (band forms >10%) on manual differential blood count.

entities.name: Moderate Thrombocytopenia
entities.description: Platelet count depressed between 50,000 and 100,000/uL on admission complete blood count.

entities.name: Severe Thrombocytopenia
entities.description: Platelet count severely depressed below 30,000-50,000/uL indicating multiorgan microvascular failure.

entities.name: Moderate Transaminitis
entities.description: Serum AST and ALT elevations 2- to 5-fold above the upper limit of normal.

entities.name: Disproportionate AST Elevation
entities.description: Serum aspartate aminotransferase level exceeding alanine aminotransferase level (AST/ALT ratio > 1).

entities.name: Elevated Alkaline Phosphatase
entities.description: Mild-to-moderate elevation of serum alkaline phosphatase (1.5- to 3-fold ULN).

entities.name: Mild Conjugated Hyperbilirubinemia
entities.description: Total bilirubin elevated between 1.5 and 4.0 mg/dL with direct fraction predominance.

entities.name: Elevated Serum Creatinine
entities.description: Serum creatinine elevated above baseline (>1.4-2.0 mg/dL) at initial admission triage.

entities.name: Elevated Blood Urea
entities.description: Blood urea nitrogen elevated above normal limits reflecting acute azotemia and tissue catabolism.

entities.name: Hypoalbuminemia
entities.description: Serum albumin depressed below 3.0-3.5 g/dL resulting from systemic capillary hyperpermeability.

entities.name: Elevated C-Reactive Protein
entities.description: Serum C-reactive protein markedly increased (>50-100 mg/L) at hospital presentation.

entities.name: Elevated Erythrocyte Sedimentation
entities.description: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate elevated above 40-60 mm/hr indicating acute vascular inflammation.

entities.name: Extreme Hyperferritinemia
entities.description: Serum ferritin level markedly elevated above 1,000-5,000 ng/mL.

entities.name: Elevated Serum Lactate
entities.description: Arterial or venous lactate elevated (>2.0-4.0 mmol/L) reflecting microcirculatory hypoperfusion.

entities.name: Elevated Creatine Kinase
entities.description: Serum creatine phosphokinase elevated above normal limits indicating myopathic injury.

entities.name: Elevated Troponin T
entities.description: Cardiac troponin I or T detectable or elevated above reference cutoffs.

entities.name: Prolonged Prothrombin Time
entities.description: Prothrombin time / INR elevated beyond reference limits indicating coagulopathy.

entities.name: Elevated D-Dimer
entities.description: Serum D-dimer markedly increased reflecting fibrin degradation and microvascular thrombosis.

entities.name: Microscopic Hematuria
entities.description: Urinalysis demonstrating microscopic red blood cells (>5 RBCs/high-power field).

entities.name: Mild Proteinuria
entities.description: Urinary dipstick protein 1+ to 2+ (30 to 100 mg/dL) without gross nephrotic range loss.

entities.name: Granular Urinary Casts
entities.description: Muddy brown coarse granular casts on urinary sediment examination.

entities.name: CSF Lymphocytic Pleocytosis
entities.description: Cerebrospinal fluid white cell count mildly elevated (10-100 cells/uL) with mononuclear predominance.

entities.name: Elevated CSF Protein
entities.description: Cerebrospinal fluid protein elevated between 60 and 200 mg/dL.

entities.name: Rapid Defervescence Response
entities.description: Complete fever defervescence and symptomatic resolution occurring within 24 to 48 hours of starting doxycycline.

entities.name: Reticulonodular Interstitial Infiltrates
entities.description: Chest radiography showing bilateral reticular and fine reticulonodular interstitial opacities.

entities.name: Bilateral Basal Infiltrates
entities.description: Chest radiography demonstrating bibasilar patchy airspace opacities and peribronchovascular thickening.

entities.name: Kerley B Lines
entities.description: Horizontal peripheral linear septal opacities at the lateral lung bases on plain chest radiograph.

entities.name: Bilateral Pleural Effusions
entities.description: Blunting of bilateral costophrenic sulci on chest radiography or fluid stripes on ultrasound.

entities.name: POCUS Splenomegaly
entities.description: Bedside point-of-care ultrasound confirming spleen bipolar length greater than 12 cm.

entities.name: POCUS Hepatomegaly
entities.description: Bedside sonographic confirmation of liver craniocaudal dimension exceeding 15 cm with normal echotexture.

entities.name: Acalculous Gallbladder Thickening
entities.description: Bedside ultrasound showing gallbladder wall edema (>3 mm) without intraluminal calculi or sludge.

entities.name: Ground-Glass Opacities
entities.description: High-resolution chest CT showing bilateral patchy ground-glass attenuation without architectural distortion.

entities.name: Interlobular Septal Thickening
entities.description: Chest CT imaging demonstrating smooth interstitial septal thickening throughout dependent pulmonary zones.

entities.name: Preserved Biliary Ducts
entities.description: Bedside abdominal sonography confirming normal caliber of intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts.

entities.name: Diffuse Myocardial Hypokinesia
entities.description: Bedside echocardiography revealing global left ventricular systolic dysfunction without focal wall motion defects.

entities.name: Minimal Pericardial Effusion
entities.description: Echocardiographic detection of a small circumferential fluid layer without hemodynamic chamber collapse.

entities.name: Leptotrombidium Mite Larva
entities.description: Microscopic six-legged larval stage of trombiculid mites (chiggers), the exclusive vector and reservoir.

entities.name: Leptotrombidium deliense
entities.description: Predominant species of trombiculid mite vector responsible for transmission in tropical Southeast Asia.

entities.name: Leptotrombidium akamushi
entities.description: Classical mite vector species distributed across Japan and temperate East Asia.

entities.name: Leptotrombidium fletcheri
entities.description: Trombiculid mite vector species adapted to rubber plantations and tropical secondary vegetation.

entities.name: Secondary Scrub Vegetation
entities.description: Regrowth brush, grassland, and transitional scrub forming localized focal 'scrub typhus islands'.

entities.name: Tsutsugamushi Triangle
entities.description: Vast geographic endemic zone encompassing Asia-Pacific, from Pakistan to Japan and northern Australia.

entities.name: Agricultural Rice Fields
entities.description: Cultivated wet or dry paddy fields serving as common sites for chigger bite exposure during farming.

entities.name: Overgrown Riverbanks
entities.description: Moist riparian vegetation along streams and irrigation ditches supporting high chigger larval density.

entities.name: Monsoon Season
entities.description: Annual period of heavy rainfall and high humidity that promotes larval chigger emergence.

entities.name: Deforested Land Clearings
entities.description: Cleared forest margins undergoing secondary vegetative regrowth where mite colonies proliferate.

entities.name: Wild Rodent Reservoirs
entities.description: Small field mammals (Rattus and Apodemus species) that serve as hosts for chigger feeding and maintenance.

entities.name: Agricultural Field Workers
entities.description: Farmers, planters, and weeders working in close direct physical contact with scrub vegetation.

entities.name: Military Field Troops
entities.description: Armed forces personnel undergoing field bivouacking, tactical maneuvers, or jungle patrols.

entities.name: Forestry Laborers
entities.description: Loggers, woodcutters, and forest rangers entering dense secondary brush and woodland areas.

entities.name: Outdoor Recreational Campers
entities.description: Hikers, campers, and trekkers sitting, resting, or sleeping on bare ground or grassy clearings.

entities.name: Rural Endemic Inhabitants
entities.description: Long-term residents of rural villages bordering bushland, riverbanks, or unmanaged scrub vegetation.

entities.name: Squatting Agricultural Posture
entities.description: Working in a low squatting position in dry fields, which brings groin and waistline close to soil.

entities.name: Elderly Rural Populations
entities.description: Older rural individuals who experience higher disease severity, complications, and mortality.

entities.name: Pregnant Women
entities.description: Expectant mothers infected during pregnancy at risk for preterm birth, miscarriage, and maternal morbidity.

entities.name: Ten-Day Incubation Period
entities.description: Typical median incubation interval of 10 to 12 days between chigger bite inoculation and acute fever.

entities.name: Six-Day Minimal Incubation
entities.description: Shortest documented incubation timeframe of 6 days following high-inoculum chigger bite.

entities.name: Twenty-One-Day Maximal Incubation
entities.description: Upper clinical latency boundary of 21 days from rural chigger exposure to acute fever onset.

entities.name: Zero Human Transmission
entities.description: Absence of direct person-to-person spread via respiratory droplets, bodily fluids, or casual contact.

entities.name: Doxycycline Refractoriness
entities.description: Persistence of high fever beyond 48 to 72 hours of therapeutic oral or IV doxycycline.

entities.name: Azithromycin Refractoriness
entities.description: Failure of clinical improvement within 72 hours of appropriate therapeutic azithromycin administration.

entities.name: Profound Leukopenia
entities.description: Marked reduction in total white blood cell count (<3,000/uL) typical of severe acute arboviral infection.

entities.name: Critical Phase Hemoconcentration
entities.description: Rapid rise in hematocrit >= 20% coinciding with fever defervescence, hallmark of dengue plasma leakage.

entities.name: Purulent Cutaneous Ulcer
entities.description: Skin ulceration producing gross pus, fluctuance, or foul exudate incompatible with dry rickettsial eschar.

entities.name: Gross Pyuria
entities.description: Urine filled with clumps of neutrophils and bacterial rods (>10^5 CFU/mL) indicating bacterial UTI.

entities.name: Intraerythrocytic Parasitemia
entities.description: Microscopic visualization of Plasmodium ring forms, trophozoites, or schizonts in peripheral blood smear.

entities.name: Extreme Direct Hyperbilirubinemia
entities.description: Marked conjugated hyperbilirubinemia (>15-25 mg/dL) with deep bronze icterus typical of severe Weil disease.

entities.name: Absence Endemic Exposure
entities.description: Zero lifetime travel or residence in known scrub typhus endemic geographic regions or rural brush habitats.

entities.name: Gram-Positive Blood Bacteremia
entities.description: Automated blood culture positivity yielding staphylococci, streptococci, or enterococci within 24-48 hours.

entities.name: Cavitary Pulmonary Lesions
entities.description: Thick-walled cavitary lesions or necrotic lung breakdown on plain chest radiograph or CT imaging.

entities.name: Centripetal Vesicular Rash
entities.description: Pruritic exanthem appearing in successive crops of teardrop vesicles on an erythematous base (varicella pattern).

entities.name: Prominent Splenic Infarction
entities.description: Wedge-shaped hypoechoic splenic parenchymal infarction on abdominal ultrasound or contrast-enhanced CT.

entities.name: Immediate One-Day Incubation
entities.description: Fever and constitutional symptoms developing within less than 24 to 48 hours of initial outdoor brush exposure.

entities.name: Prolonged Multi-Month Incubation
entities.description: Latency period exceeding 30 to 60 days between rural travel return and acute febrile illness onset.

entities.name: Purulent Conjunctival Discharge
entities.description: Copious thick yellow or green purulent ocular drainage and crusting of the eyelids.

entities.name: Marked Generalized Lymphadenopathy Absence
entities.description: Complete absence of lymph node enlargement in a patient presenting with high fever and non-specific rash.

entities.name: Isolated Unconjugated Hyperbilirubinemia
entities.description: Elevated indirect bilirubin with normal direct bilirubin and normal liver transaminases.

entities.name: Beta-Lactam Responsiveness
entities.description: Rapid clinical cure and fever defervescence following administration of ampicillin, ceftriaxone, or meropenem.

entities.name: Fluoroquinolone Responsiveness
entities.description: Prompt resolution of fever within 24-48 hours of ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin monotherapy.

entities.name: Marked Eosinophilia
entities.description: Absolute eosinophil count >1,500/uL on differential complete blood count.

entities.name: Normal C-Reactive Protein
entities.description: Serum C-reactive protein within strictly normal limits (<5 mg/L) during severe acute febrile illness.

entities.name: Dengue Fever
entities.description: Mosquito-borne arboviral illness characterized by retro-orbital pain, leukopenia, and defervescence plasma leak.

entities.name: Severe Dengue
entities.description: Severe dengue virus infection marked by plasma leakage, severe hemorrhage, shock, and pleural effusions at defervescence.

entities.name: Leptospirosis
entities.description: Zoonotic spirochetal infection transmitted by rodent urine in floodwaters, causing severe calf pain and jaundice.

entities.name: Severe Leptospirosis
entities.description: Weil disease presenting with catastrophic triad of deep jaundice, oliguric renal failure, and pulmonary hemorrhage.

entities.name: Falciparum Malaria
entities.description: Protozoan infection caused by Plasmodium falciparum, characterized by cyclic paroxysms and intraerythrocytic rings.

entities.name: Vivax Malaria
entities.description: Benign tertian malaria caused by Plasmodium vivax presenting with 48-hour paroxysmal rigors and splenomegaly.

entities.name: Murine Typhus
entities.description: Flea-borne rickettsiosis caused by Rickettsia typhi associated with commensal rats in urban and port environments.

entities.name: Typhoid Fever
entities.description: Enteric fever caused by Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi presenting with stepladder fever and rose spots.

entities.name: Melioidosis
entities.description: Saprophytic environmental bacterial infection caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei in tropical soils.

entities.name: Spotted Fever Rickettsiosis
entities.description: Tick-borne rickettsial disease caused by Rickettsia rickettsii or R. conorii presenting with centripetal petechiae.

entities.name: Infectious Mononucleosis
entities.description: Epstein-Barr virus infection presenting with exudative tonsillopharyngitis, fatigue, and atypical lymphocytosis.

entities.name: Primary HIV Infection
entities.description: Acute retroviral seroconversion illness presenting with fever, maculopapular rash, and painful aphthous ulcers.

entities.name: Meningococcal Disease
entities.description: Fulminant invasive Neisseria meningitidis infection causing purpura fulminans and purulent meningitis.

entities.name: Japanese Encephalitis
entities.description: Mosquito-borne flavivirus causing acute encephalitis with parkinsonian features and thalamic lesions.

entities.name: Community-Acquired Pneumonia
entities.description: Bacterial lung parenchyma infection typically caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae with lobar consolidation.

entities.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
entities.description: Rodent-borne viral zoonosis causing rapid noncardiogenic pulmonary edema with immunoblasts and hemoconcentration.

entities.name: Cutaneous Anthrax
entities.description: Zoonotic infection caused by Bacillus anthracis spores presenting with painless black eschar and massive gelatinous edema.

relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute febrile illness presents abruptly with high remittent or continuous fever, rigors, and debilitating constitutional prostration.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Noncardiogenic pulmonary edema arises from diffuse microvascular capillary leakage and endothelial injury in the pulmonary circulation.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Acute respiratory distress syndrome develops during the second week of untreated illness due to catastrophic alveolar-capillary barrier breakdown.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Interstitial pneumonitis manifests with non-productive cough, tachypnea, and fine bilateral crepitations caused by septal endothelial inflammation.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Acute kidney injury occurs in 20-40% of hospitalized patients due to a combination of renal hypoperfusion and microvascular endothelial injury.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Acute tubular necrosis complicates severe scrub typhus shock, causing oliguric renal failure with characteristic granular muddy brown casts.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Acute interstitial nephritis represents direct Orientia-mediated peritubular endothelial inflammation leading to sterile pyuria and azotemia.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Aseptic meningoencephalitis presents with neck stiffness, headache, confusion, and lymphocytic cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Aseptic meningitis results from microvascular leptomeningeal inflammation manifesting with nuchal rigidity and mononuclear CSF pleocytosis.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Encephalopathy occurs in severe scrub typhus secondary to cerebral microvascular perivascular cuffing and toxic cytokine release.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Infectious myocarditis manifests with chest discomfort, conduction abnormalities, sinus tachycardia, or cardiogenic shock.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Cardiogenic shock complicates fulminant scrub typhus myocarditis, leading to hypotension refractory to fluid administration.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Septic shock develops in severe disseminated vasculitis due to profound systemic vasodilatation and capillary leakage.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Multiorgan dysfunction syndrome combines pulmonary, renal, hepatic, and hematological failure, carrying high untreated mortality.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Disseminated intravascular coagulation results from widespread endothelial injury, presenting with petechiae, mucosal bleeding, and prolonged PT/INR.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Acute pericarditis arises from serosal microvascular involvement and can accompany infectious myocarditis as perimyocarditis.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Pericardial effusion is detectable on bedside echocardiography as an anechoic fluid stripe in up to 10-25% of complicated cases.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Generalized lymphadenopathy reflects systemic reticuloendothelial proliferation following initial localized sentinel node enlargement.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Splenomegaly is present in 30-50% of patients and is readily identified by palpation or bedside ultrasound.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Hepatomegaly manifests as a smooth, tender liver edge palpable 2 to 4 cm below the right costal margin.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Acute hepatitis develops in over 80% of scrub typhus cases, causing mild-to-moderate transaminase elevations and mild hepatomegaly.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Canalicular cholestasis presents with mild conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and elevated serum alkaline phosphatase without biliary dilation.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Gastrointestinal mucosal hemorrhage occurs in severe scrub typhus manifesting as hematemesis, melena, or occult fecal blood loss.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Multiple gastric ulcers develop secondary to microvascular thrombosis and mucosal ischemia in severe systemic infection.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Acute pancreatitis occurs rarely as a manifestation of peripancreatic microvascular ischemia and systemic endothelial inflammation.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Severe frontal cephalalgia is nearly universal (90-95%) in acute scrub typhus, often described as throbbing and resistant to common analgesics.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Retro-orbital pain accompanies acute cephalalgia and conjunctival suffusion during the early bacteremic phase.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Generalized myalgia reflects diffuse intramuscular capillary angiitis and systemic cytokine release.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Peripheral polyneuropathy presents as symmetrical sensory loss, paresthesias, or motor weakness during prolonged or convalescent disease.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Acute transient deafness develops in 20-35% of scrub typhus patients due to eighth cranial nerve or cochlear microvasculitis.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Tinnitus serves as a valuable early diagnostic clue preceding or accompanying sensorineural hearing loss in scrub typhus.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Cranial nerve palsy can manifest as facial nerve paresis, abducens palsy, or auditory impairment resulting from focal microvascular ischemia.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Cerebral angiitis leads to focal neurological deficits, confusion, and localized ischemic brain changes on neuroimaging.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Generalized seizures can occur in pediatric or severe adult cases complicated by acute meningoencephalitis.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Oliguria indicates worsening acute kidney injury and hypoperfusion in patients developing multiorgan failure.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Pleuritic chest pain arises from localized pleuritis and peripheral pulmonary interstitial infiltrates.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Exudative pleural effusion frequently accompanies interstitial pneumonitis in scrub typhus, appearing bilaterally or unilaterally.
